title: The live engine wrote listing files into the container image layer

first_order.what_broke: On the running Fly machine 80d34da6636478, listing and pricing-rationale files were written to /app/store instead of the volume at /data/store. /app is the image layer and every deploy erases it. A listing file is what puts a pack on the shelf, so those packs would have silently left the shelf on the next deploy.
first_order.receipt: fly ssh console -a prospector-engine -C 'find /app/store -type f' returned 8 files at 21:20Z on 2026-08-18, including /app/store/listings/aee5f8f26657c9b0.json

cause_chain: paths.store_root() read PROSPECTOR_STORE_ROOT, which nothing outside the test suite sets, and fell back to a path derived from __file__.
Two resolvers existed for one concept: config.store_root() reads PROSPECTOR_STORE_DIR and is the one the plists and the Fly machine set.

A rule written as prose with no sweep and no guard. On 2026-08-17 four __file__-derived store constants were fixed and the rule was written into CLAUDE.md. Nothing searched for a fifth, and nothing would have failed if one existed.

The sweep for siblings was a regex over single lines, and the bug's normal shape spans two lines. So the sweep reported 2 where an AST walk reports 40, and the record closed on a number that was measuring something else.

CLASS: a sibling sweep written as a regex can only find the instances that happen to share the syntax of the one that was noticed. When the defect is semantic - a value derived from the wrong source - the sweep has to be semantic too, or the count it produces is not a measure of the class, and a low count reads as containment.

2026-08-20. The class recurred one level up, inside the mechanism written to close it. The AST guard tracks NAMES, which is why it saw the two-step form, but it was pinned to the one EXPRESSION it had been shown: a division of a file-derived name by 'store'. Three more syntaxes were on disk with it green - os.path.join(dirname(__file__), 'store', ...) in tools/backfill_pack_currency.py:56, ROOT.glob('store/ops/restore_drill*') in scripts/ops_status.py:199, and a module's __file__ rather than the current one in tests/invariants/test_audit_isolation.py:22. It also never looked at the OTHER way to name the wrong store: a bare 'store/...' resolved against the process working directory, which under the engine image (WORKDIR /app, deploy/engine/Dockerfile:55) is the image layer this incident is about. 17 of those were on disk. CLASS, restated: a guard that enumerates syntaxes is a regex with a longer reach. It has to be written against the SEMANTIC question - where does this path come from - and every syntax that answers it wrongly has to be enumerated on purpose, with a test per syntax that fails when the rule for it is removed.

second_order.note:
CORRECTED 2026-08-19. This field read 2. An AST walk of the repo found 40 expressions joining a __file__-derived path with a store or storage segment. The original sweep was a regex over ONE LINE, and almost every real offender is written in two steps: `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` on one line and `ROOT / "store" / "dossiers"` on another. A regex over one line cannot see a name bound on another, so the count was not slightly low, it was measuring a different thing. 30 were rewritten to prospector.config.store_root(); the writers among them were tools/retire_rotted_passes.py (manifest and the sqlite DB), tools/sweep_shelf_copy.py, tools/recover_stranded_passes.py, four backfills under tools/ and two under scripts/, and store_platform/scripts/backfill_facets.py. The readers were scripts/ops_state.py, scripts/ops_status.py, scripts/store_audit.py, scripts/watch_engine.py, scripts/unit_economics.py, scripts/pack_banner_probe.py, tools/meta_shape_monitor.py and seven sites across five files under tools/experiments/. The remaining 10 are on an allow-list, each with the reason it is correct: the resolver itself, the migration tool that must run without the package, the tracked repo ledger under storage/, and four fences that name the repo store in order to prove nothing was written there. Tracked as issue #371.

CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-20, and the correction is the same shape as the first one. 40 was the count of ONE syntax. Extending the walk to os.path.join, to a .glob()/.rglob()/.joinpath() off a file-derived name, and to a module's __file__ adds 3. A second walk for the working-directory form - a string whose first path SEGMENT is store or storage, passed as the first argument to a call that turns a string into a path - finds 17 more: prospector/human_review.py:50, prospector/numeric_citation.py:657, prospector/prescreen_prefilter.py:430, run_v2.py:159, tools/build_sample_fixture.py:375, tools/publish_offline.py:34, tools/publish_passes.py:230, tools/reprice_to_charm_rungs.py:69, tools/experiments/d5_corroboration.py:53, tools/experiments/q4b_live_catalogue_exposure.py:89, four scripts under tools/experiments/w0_free_prescreen_auc/, tests/invariants/test_audit_isolation.py:21, tests/ops/cc/test_ephemeral_jobs.py:80 and tests/unit/test_adaptive_persona.py:17. 16 of the 17 were rewritten; the last is a dummy attribute on a mock that never reaches a filesystem. Module-level path CONSTANTS became functions, so the resolver is read on every call rather than bound at import, which is the trap prescreen_prefilter.py:412 already documents. Four exemptions were added with their reasons: storage/durable_ledger.md is a tracked repo artifact that must move with the code, two suite fences must name the repo-local store to prove the suite left it alone, and the mock above.

third_order.mechanism:
tests/unit/test_no_store_path_is_derived_from_file.py walks every .py in the repo as an AST, collects the module-level names bound to any expression mentioning __file__, and fails on any division of such a name by the string 'store' or 'storage'. It sees the two-step form the original regex could not, and it will see a third form because it tracks names rather than matching text. The allow-list is a dict of path -> reason: a further test asserts every allowed file still contains an offender, so an entry cannot outlive its reason and quietly exempt the next one written there, and another asserts each reason is long enough to be one. There is an anti-vacuity test on the source walk itself. Mutation-checked: restoring `MANIFEST = ROOT / "store" / "retired_passes.json"` in tools/retire_rotted_passes.py turns it red.

The test this record originally landed, tests/unit/test_one_store_resolver.py::test_no_third_resolver_appears, is named for this check and does not perform it: it asserts the two KNOWN resolvers agree and never looks for a third. That is the S1 class from ADR 0002, a check that cannot fail, inside the mechanism for a different incident.

2026-08-20, second mechanism. tests/unit/test_no_store_path_is_relative_to_the_cwd.py is a separate file on purpose: the two failures have different fixes and different correct exceptions, and one shared allow-list would let either excuse the other. It flags a string whose first path SEGMENT is store or storage passed as the first argument to Path/open/glob.glob/os.path.join and the rest of that set, and nothing else - tmp_path / 'store' is correct and common, parts[0] == 'store' is a comparison, store_platform/ is a different segment, and a guard that fired on any of those would earn an allow-list long enough to hide a real one. Both files now carry a parametrised test per syntax they are supposed to catch AND per shape they must not flag, so removing a rule fails a named test instead of silently shrinking the guard. The __file__ guard also stopped firing on function PARAMETERS: one root = Path(__file__)... inside any function had made the name root file-derived for that whole file, and reported tests/unit/test_console_tools_run.py:359 - def _tree(root: Path), always called with tmp_path - as an offender. Mutation-checked, eight of them: reverting any of four real sites, and deleting any of four guard rules, turns a green guard red.

grade.signature: a store path that comes from anywhere other than config.store_root(): derived from __file__, or relative to the process working directory
